en: to have a crick; to feel a stitch

examples.en: I overdid my workout yesterday, so I have a stitch in my side.

examples.ko: 잠을 잘못 잤는지 목이 결려서 고개를 못 돌려요.
examples.en: I must have slept wrong; my neck is stiff and I can't turn my head.

examples.ko: 숨을 크게 쉬면 가슴이 결리는 느낌이에요.
examples.en: When I breathe deeply, my chest feels like it catches.
After sitting for a long time, my back got a crick.
When your lower back is cricked, apply a warm compress.
Even though my shoulder hurts, I can't be bothered to go to the hospital.

explain: '아프다'와 달리 숨을 쉬거나 움직일 때 걸리는 듯 찌릿한 느낌에 써요. 아픈 부위가 주어라서 '옆구리가 결리다', '어깨가 결리다'처럼 말해요. 비슷하게 '담이 걸리다'라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '아프다', it describes a catching, twinging feeling when you breathe or move. The sore body part is the subject, as in '옆구리가 결리다' or '어깨가 결리다'. People also say '담이 걸리다' for a similar feeling.

examples.en: I always wear rubber gloves when doing dishes.
The rubber gloves tore, so I bought new ones.
My hands got rough, so I clean wearing rubber gloves.
Water got inside the rubber gloves.
Mom, where are the rubber gloves?
I made kimchi wearing red rubber gloves.

explain: '장갑을 끼다/벗다'처럼 '끼다'와 함께 써요. 설거지나 청소, 김장할 때 쓰는 두꺼운 장갑이라서 얇은 '비닐장갑'과 구분해요.
explain_en: Use it with '끼다' and '벗다', as in '장갑을 끼다'. It is a thick glove for dishes, cleaning and kimchi making, so it is distinguished from thin '비닐장갑'.

examples.en: The smell is so bad that I feel nauseous.
I rode in the car for a long time and now I feel nauseous.

examples.ko: 그 장면을 보고 구역질이 날 것 같았어요.
examples.en: I felt like gagging when I saw that scene.
I opened the window to hold back the nausea.

examples.ko: 이틀 전부터 구역질이 나고 입맛이 없어요.
examples.en: Since two days ago, I've felt nauseous and have had no appetite.
After taking the medicine, the nausea stopped.

explain: 토할 것처럼 속이 울렁거리고 헛구역질이 나는 느낌이에요. 실제로 토하는 건 '토하다'이고, '속이 안 좋다'나 '메스껍다'는 더 부드러운 말이에요. 아주 싫은 것을 보았을 때도 '구역질이 나다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the feeling of your stomach heaving as if you will vomit. Actually throwing up is '토하다', while '속이 안 좋다' and '메스껍다' are softer. People also say '구역질이 나다' when they find something disgusting.

examples.ko: 저는 어릴 때부터 근시라서 안경을 써요.
examples.en: I have been nearsighted since I was little, so I wear glasses.
If you look at a smartphone for a long time, nearsightedness gets worse.
I had a nearsightedness test at the eye clinic.

examples.ko: 근시인 사람은 멀리 있는 글씨가 흐리게 보여요.
examples.en: For nearsighted people, far-away letters look blurry.
I heard nearsightedness in children is increasing every year.

examples.ko: 약한 근시는 렌즈로 쉽게 교정할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Mild nearsightedness is easy to correct with lenses.

explain: '근시'는 가까운 것은 잘 보이고 먼 것은 흐리게 보이는 눈이에요. 반대로 먼 것은 보이고 가까운 것이 흐린 눈은 '원시'라고 해요. 보통 '근시예요', '근시라서 안경을 써요'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: 근시 is an eye condition where near things look clear and far things look blurry. The opposite, where far things are clear and near ones are blurry, is 원시. People usually say 근시예요 or 근시라서 안경을 써요.

examples.ko: 옛날에는 아이들 배 속에 기생충이 많았어요.
examples.en: In the past, many children had parasites in their stomachs.

examples.ko: 생선을 날로 먹으면 기생충에 걸릴 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you eat raw fish, you can get parasites.

examples.ko: 기생충 약을 먹고 병원에서 검사를 받았어요.
examples.en: I took anti-parasite medicine and got a test at the hospital.
Puppies also need a parasite check.

examples.ko: 어떤 기생충은 다른 동물의 몸에서 살아요.
examples.en: Some parasites live inside another animal's body.
I watched the film 'Parasite' at a movie theater.

explain: 몸 안팎에 붙어서 사는 벌레를 말해요. 사람에게 '기생충 같다'고 하면 남에게 기대어 사는 사람을 심하게 낮추는 말이니 조심해야 해요. 영화 「기생충」 덕분에 외국 사람에게도 익숙한 단어가 됐어요.
explain_en: It means worms and creatures that live on or inside a body. Calling a person '기생충 같다' insults someone who lives off others, so be careful. The film 'Parasite' made the word familiar to foreigners.

en: to be haggard; to be emaciated

examples.en: My younger brother is a bit prickly today.
My skin was dry and rough because I couldn't sleep.
He's a prickly person, so it's hard to talk to him.
Everyone will get irritable during exam period.
When my friend is hungry, he gets snippy and curt.
The team leader was sharp in the meeting, so I got nervous.

explain: 사람에게 쓰면 '예민하고 말이 날카롭다'는 느낌이고, 피부나 수염에 쓰면 '거칠고 윤기가 없다'는 뜻이에요. 살이 빠져 수척해 보이는 얼굴에도 써요. '화나다'처럼 한순간의 감정이 아니라 계속되는 태도에 가까워요. '까칠남', '까칠녀'처럼도 써요.
explain_en: For people, 까칠하다 means sharp, touchy, and hard to please; for skin or stubble it means rough and lacking moisture. It can also describe a thin, worn-out face. Unlike 화나다, it is a lasting attitude rather than a momentary feeling. It also appears as 까칠남 and 까칠녀.

examples.en: I fell on the icy road and hurt my tailbone.

examples.ko: 꼬리뼈가 아파서 오래 앉아 있기 힘들어요.
examples.en: My tailbone hurts, so it's hard to sit for long.

examples.ko: 의자에 앉을 때 꼬리뼈가 눌려서 쿠션을 깔았어요.
examples.en: My tailbone got pressed when I sat, so I put a cushion down.
I landed hard on my bottom, and now my tailbone throbs.

examples.ko: 병원에서 꼬리뼈 사진을 찍어 보자고 했어요.
examples.en: At the hospital they said let's take an X-ray of the tailbone.
Humans have a tailbone, but no tail.

explain: 넘어져서 엉덩이를 세게 다쳤을 때 '꼬리뼈가 아프다'라고 구체적으로 말해요. 병원에서도 이렇게 설명하면 잘 통해요.
explain_en: When you fall and hurt your bottom, people say specifically '꼬리뼈가 아프다'. Describing it this way also works well at a hospital.

examples.ko: 하루 종일 에어컨 바람을 쐬었더니 냉방병에 걸렸어요.
examples.en: After being in the air conditioning all day, I came down with air-conditioning sickness.

examples.ko: 냉방병 때문에 머리가 아프고 몸이 으슬으슬해요.
examples.en: Because of air-conditioning sickness, I have a headache and the chills.
Lots of people get air-conditioning sickness in the office.

examples.ko: 냉방병을 막으려면 실내 온도를 너무 낮추지 마세요.
examples.en: To prevent air-conditioning sickness, don't set the room temperature too low.

examples.ko: 여름 감기가 사실은 냉방병일 수도 있어요.
examples.en: What seems like a summer cold could actually be air-conditioning sickness.

examples.ko: 냉방병에 걸리지 않게 얇은 겉옷을 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I brought a thin jacket so I wouldn't get air-conditioning sickness.

explain: 더운 바깥과 시원한 실내의 온도 차이 때문에 감기처럼 몸이 안 좋을 때 써요. 보통 '냉방병에 걸리다'라고 말해요. 여름에 자주 듣는 말이에요.
explain_en: It refers to feeling unwell, like a cold, because of the temperature gap between the hot outdoors and the cool indoors. People usually say '냉방병에 걸리다'. It is a word you hear a lot in summer.

examples.ko: 무릎 구멍 난 곳에 천을 덧댔어요.
examples.en: I patched the hole at the knee with a piece of cloth.
I put plastic over the window to keep out the cold.

examples.ko: 낡은 신발 밑창에 고무를 덧대서 신어요.
examples.en: I add rubber to the sole of my worn-out shoes and wear them.

examples.ko: 상처 위에 거즈를 덧대고 붕대를 감았어요.
examples.en: I laid gauze over the wound and wrapped a bandage.
Please put a wooden splint on the broken leg.
I came to buy cloth to patch jeans with.

explain: 구멍이나 약한 곳 위에 천, 판 같은 것을 한 겹 더 대는 거예요. '덧붙이다'는 말이나 내용을 더할 때 많이 쓰고, '덧대다'는 물건을 겉에 대는 데 써요.
explain_en: It means laying another layer, such as cloth or a board, over a hole or weak spot. '덧붙이다' is commonly used for adding words or content, while '덧대다' is for putting a physical item on the surface.

en: to hiccup; to have the hiccups

examples.en: My younger brother keeps hiccuping.
I hiccuped during class and was embarrassed.
The hiccuping baby was so cute that I watched for a while.
I hiccuped while drinking soda.
I held my breath so I wouldn't hiccup.
If you hiccup while laughing, it's even funnier.

explain: '딸꾹질이 나요'가 더 자주 들려요. '딸꾹질해요'는 지금 계속하고 있는 모습을 말할 때 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 딸꾹질이 나요 is heard more often. 딸꾹질해요 sounds natural when you describe someone who is hiccuping right now.

examples.en: The baby got heat rash on the neck.

examples.ko: 더운 날 땀띠 때문에 너무 가려워요.
examples.en: On hot days, the heat rash makes me very itchy.

examples.ko: 땀띠에는 시원하게 씻고 말려 주는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: For heat rash, it's good to wash coolly and dry the skin.

examples.ko: 땀띠 연고를 바르니까 가려운 게 나아졌어요.
examples.en: After I put heat rash ointment on, the itching got better.

examples.ko: 땀띠 가루를 발라 주니 아기가 편안해 보여요.
examples.en: After I put powder on the heat rash, the baby looks comfortable.
They say heat rash forms when sweat pores get blocked.

explain: 더운 여름에 땀이 많이 나서 피부에 작게 돋는 발진이에요. 보통 '땀띠가 나다'라고 말하고, 아기들에게 많아서 '땀띠 가루'도 같이 알아 두면 좋아요.
explain_en: It is a small skin rash that appears when you sweat a lot in hot summer. People usually say '땀띠가 나다', and since it is common in babies, '땀띠 가루' (heat rash powder) is a good word to know too.

examples.ko: 비행기가 높이 올라가면 기압이 낮아져서 귀가 먹먹해져요.
examples.en: When a plane climbs high, the air pressure drops and my ears feel blocked.

examples.ko: 건물 안에서 누군가의 울음소리가 새어 나와서 가슴이 먹먹했어요.
examples.en: Someone's crying leaked out from inside the building and my chest felt heavy.
Maybe I have a cold, my ears feel stuffed.

examples.ko: 수영을 하고 나왔더니 귀가 먹먹한데 물이 들어갔나 봐요.
examples.en: My ears feel blocked after swimming. Maybe water got in.

examples.ko: 슬픈 영화를 보고 나니 가슴이 먹먹해서 말이 안 나왔어요.
examples.en: After the sad movie my chest felt so heavy that I couldn't speak.
When we entered the tunnel, my ears felt blocked.

explain: 귀에 쓰면 물이나 기압 때문에 소리가 잘 안 들리고 막힌 느낌이에요. 가슴에 쓰면 슬픔이나 감동이 가득 차서 말이 잘 안 나오는 느낌이에요. 귀가 막힌 느낌은 '멍멍하다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: With ears, it means a blocked, muffled feeling where sounds are hard to hear because of water or pressure. With the chest, it means sadness or emotion fills you so much that words won't come. The blocked-ear feeling can also be called '멍멍하다'.

examples.en: I hurt my leg, so I get around on crutches.
Stairs are hard because of the crutches.
I'm happy that I can walk without crutches now.
My friend came to school on crutches.
I learned how to use crutches at the hospital.

examples.ko: 목발을 짚은 사람에게 문을 잡아 줬어요.
examples.en: I held the door for a person on crutches.

explain: 다리가 아파서 걸을 때 겨드랑이에 끼고 짚는 지팡이예요. '목발을 짚다', '목발을 쓰다'처럼 말해요. 손으로 잡는 '지팡이'와는 다르게 몸을 받쳐 주는 도구로 생각하면 돼요.
explain_en: These are the sticks you tuck under your arms and lean on when walking with an injured leg. You say '목발을 짚다' or '목발을 쓰다'. Unlike a '지팡이' (cane) held in the hand, think of them as a tool that supports your body weight.

examples.ko: 새 신발을 신었더니 발에 물집이 생겼어요.
examples.en: I wore new shoes and got a blister on my foot.

examples.ko: 뜨거운 물에 데어서 손에 물집이 났어요.
examples.en: I got scalded by hot water and a blister came up on my hand.

examples.ko: 물집은 억지로 터뜨리지 않는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's best not to pop a blister by force.

examples.ko: 등산 때문에 발바닥 물집이 아파서 쉬었어요.
examples.en: The blister on my sole hurt from hiking, so I rested.
I put a bandage on the blister and kept walking.

examples.ko: 오랫동안 삽질을 했더니 손에 물집이 잡혔어요.
examples.en: After shoveling for a long time, blisters formed on my hands.

explain: 물집은 '생기다, 잡히다, 터지다'처럼 같이 쓰는 동사가 많고, '물집이 잡혔다'는 말도 자주 들어요. 피부가 쓸리거나 데면 생겨요. 피부 밑에서 피가 나 색이 변하는 '멍'과는 달라요.
explain_en: 물집 goes with many verbs, such as 생기다, 잡히다 and 터지다, and 물집이 잡혔다 is a very common phrase. It forms when skin is rubbed or burned. It differs from 멍 (a bruise), where blood under the skin changes its color.

examples.en: My child had a slight fever, so he stayed home from school.
I have a mild fever, but I'm not badly sick.
My body feels sluggish because of a slight fever.
When I took my temperature, it was only a slight fever.
A mild fever and a cough have continued for days.
In the evening I feel weak from a mild fever.

explain: 몸이 조금 뜨거운 정도의 약한 열이에요. 반대로 높은 열은 '고열'이라고 해요. 병원에서는 '미열이 있다', '미열이 나다'처럼 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is a low-grade fever where the body is only a little warm. A high fever is '고열'. At the doctor's it is said as '미열이 있다' or '미열이 나다'.

examples.ko: 아이가 제 바짓가랑이를 붙잡고 놓지 않아요.
examples.en: The child is holding on to my pant leg and won't let go.
My pant legs got completely wet because of the rain.
I rolled up my pant legs and stepped into the stream.
Your pant legs are covered in dirt.
The excited puppy kept tugging at my pant leg with its teeth.
The pant legs are so long that I keep stepping on them.

explain: 바지에서 한쪽 다리가 들어가는 부분이에요. 아이가 매달리거나 비에 젖는 장면에서 자주 나와요. 줄여서 '가랑이'라고도 하지만 몸의 다리 사이를 가리킬 수도 있어서, 옷 이야기에서는 '바짓가랑이'가 더 분명해요.

phrases.example: 취직 좀 시켜 달라고 사장님 바짓가랑이를 붙잡고 늘어졌어요.
phrases.en: I clung to the boss's pant leg and begged him to give me a job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 체면을 가리지 않고 끈질기게 부탁하거나 매달릴 때 쓰는 비유예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figure of speech for begging or clinging on persistently without caring about dignity.
phrases.en_equiv: to cling to someone and beg; to hang on and plead

explain_en: It is the part of the pants that covers one leg, and it often appears when a child clings on or the pants get wet. It can be shortened to '가랑이', but that can also mean the crotch of the body, so '바짓가랑이' is clearer when talking about clothes.

examples.en: The child has cough and fever symptoms.
They check for fever at the entrance.
If the fever continues, go to the hospital.
Even after taking medicine, the fever won't go down.
The battery shut off because of overheating.
Patients with a fever, please wait separately.

explain: 몸이나 기계에서 열이 나는 것을 말하는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상에서 사람이 아플 때는 '열이 나요'라고 하고, 병원이나 안내문에서 '발열'을 써요. 기계에는 '과열'(너무 뜨거워짐)을 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is a formal word for giving off heat, from a body or from a machine. In daily speech you say 열이 나요 when you are sick; 발열 appears in hospitals and notices. For machines that get too hot, 과열 is the common word.

examples.ko: 라면을 먹고 잤더니 얼굴에 부기가 있어요.
examples.en: I ate ramen and slept, so my face is puffy.

examples.ko: 발목을 삐어서 부기가 아직 안 빠졌어요.
examples.en: I sprained my ankle and the swelling hasn't gone down yet.

examples.ko: 얼음찜질을 하면 부기를 줄일 수 있어요.
examples.en: An ice pack can reduce swelling.
Every morning I worry about puffy eyes.

examples.ko: 수술한 뒤 일주일 동안 부기가 심했어요.
examples.en: For a week after the surgery, the swelling was severe.

examples.ko: 부기를 빼려고 물을 많이 마시고 있어요.
examples.en: I'm drinking lots of water to get rid of the puffiness.

explain: 몸이 붓는 것을 말하고, '부기가 빠지다', '부기를 빼다'처럼 동사와 함께 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '붓기'라고도 많이 해요. 같은 소리의 '부기(장부 적기)'는 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: It means swelling of the body, used as 부기가 빠지다 or 부기를 빼다. In daily talk people also say 붓기. There is another 부기 (bookkeeping) with the same sound, but it is a different word.

examples.en: Since yesterday, pimples have come up on my forehead and chin.

examples.ko: 뾰루지를 손으로 짜면 흉터가 남을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you squeeze a pimple with your hands, it can leave a scar.

examples.ko: 이마에 난 뾰루지 때문에 앞머리로 가렸어요.
examples.en: I covered the pimple on my forehead with my bangs.
A pimple usually goes down after a few days.
I bought an ointment for pimples at the pharmacy.
I don't have acne, but I get pimples sometimes.

explain: '뾰루지가 나다'라고 말해요. 여드름과 비슷하지만 피곤하거나 피부가 예민할 때 갑자기 생긴 것에도 넓게 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: You say '뾰루지가 나다'. It is similar to acne, but it is a broad word that also covers bumps that suddenly appear when you are tired or your skin is sensitive.

examples.en: My wisdom tooth is coming in and my gums hurt.
Yesterday I went to the dentist and had my wisdom tooth pulled.

examples.ko: 사랑니를 뽑고 나서 하루 종일 죽만 먹었어요.
examples.en: After getting my wisdom tooth pulled, I only ate porridge all day.

examples.ko: 사랑니는 어른이 되어서 나는 경우가 많아요.
examples.en: Wisdom teeth often come in once you're an adult.
I heard my lower wisdom tooth grew in at a slant.
It's hard to eat because of my wisdom tooth.

explain: '사랑니가 나다', '사랑니를 뽑다'가 가장 자주 쓰는 짝이에요. 치과에서는 '사랑니 발치'라고도 해요. 영어의 wisdom tooth처럼 '지혜'가 아니라 '사랑'이라는 말이 들어가서 재미있게 외울 수 있어요.
explain_en: The most common pairings are '사랑니가 나다' (a wisdom tooth comes in) and '사랑니를 뽑다' (pull a wisdom tooth). At the dentist it's also called '사랑니 발치'. Unlike English 'wisdom', the Korean word has 'love' in it, which makes it fun to remember.

examples.en: My younger sibling has had eczema since childhood.

examples.ko: 겨울에는 아토피 때문에 피부가 많이 가려워요.
examples.en: In winter, my skin gets very itchy because of eczema.

examples.ko: 아토피 피부에는 순한 비누를 쓰는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It is good to use mild soap on eczema-prone skin.
I got treatment for my eczema at the hospital and it improved a lot.

examples.ko: 이 로션은 아토피로 고생하는 아이들에게 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This lotion is popular with kids who suffer from eczema.
I heard that eczema started after moving into the new house.

explain: '아토피'는 보통 '아토피 피부염'을 줄여서 말해요. 가려움과 건조함이 특징이라 '아토피가 있다', '아토피가 생기다', '아토피가 심하다'처럼 써요. 일상에서는 '습진'보다 '아토피'를 더 자주 들어요.
explain_en: 아토피 is the everyday short form of 아토피 피부염 (atopic dermatitis). People say 아토피가 있다, 아토피가 생기다, or 아토피가 심하다. In daily talk, Koreans hear 아토피 much more often than 습진.

en: to worsen; to become worse; to deteriorate

examples.ko: 날씨가 갑자기 악화해서 비행기가 못 떠요.
examples.en: The weather suddenly worsened, so the plane can't take off.

examples.ko: 병이 악화하지 않도록 약을 꼭 드세요.
examples.en: Take your medicine so the illness doesn't get worse.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 관계가 점점 악화하고 있어요.
examples.en: Relations between the two countries are gradually worsening.

examples.ko: 건강이 악화한 뒤로 일을 쉬고 있어요.
examples.en: Since my health deteriorated, I've been taking a break from work.
If the situation gets worse, contact me right away.
Noise made my relationship with the neighbors worse.

explain: '병이 악화하다', '관계가 악화하다'처럼 주어가 스스로 나빠질 때 써요. 같은 뜻으로 '악화되다'도 쓰고, 누군가 나빠지게 만들 때는 '악화시키다'를 써요. 반대말은 '호전되다'예요.
explain_en: It is used when the subject itself gets worse, as in '병이 악화하다' and '관계가 악화하다'. '악화되다' is also used with the same meaning, and '악화시키다' is for someone making things worse. The opposite is '호전되다'.

p.n: The other form is more common in speech.

examples.en: In winter a duck-down jacket is the warmest.

examples.ko: 이 이불은 오리털이 가득 들어 있어요.
examples.en: This blanket is stuffed full of duck down.

examples.ko: 오리털 패딩을 세탁할 때는 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to be careful when washing a duck-down padded coat.
I bought a light, warm duck-down pillow.
Down feathers poked out and made the coat look messy.
Duck down is cheaper than goose down.

explain: 패딩이나 이불 속에 넣는 오리의 부드러운 털이에요. 비슷한 재료로 '거위털(구스다운)'이 있는데, 보통 더 비싸요. 옷 상표에서는 '다운'이라는 말도 같이 봐요.
explain_en: It is the soft down of ducks used to fill padded coats and blankets. A similar material is '거위털' (goose down), which is usually pricier. On clothing labels you will also see the word '다운'.

examples.en: If I sit for a long time, I get a backache.
I get physical therapy at the hospital because of back pain.

examples.ko: 아버지는 요통으로 오래 서 있기 힘드세요.
examples.en: My father finds it hard to stand for long because of lower back pain.

examples.ko: 요통에는 가벼운 걷기 운동이 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Light walking exercise helps with lower back pain.

examples.ko: 요통은 한 번 생기면 오래가기도 해요.
examples.en: Once you get lower back pain, it can sometimes last a long time.
If the back pain continues, get it checked.

explain: 일상에서는 '허리가 아프다', '허리 통증'이라고 많이 말해요. '요통'은 병원이나 건강 정보에서 더 자주 보여요. '허리'는 몸의 부위이고 '요통'은 아픈 증상을 가리켜요.
explain_en: In daily life people more often say '허리가 아프다' or '허리 통증'. '요통' appears more in hospitals and health information. '허리' is the body part, while '요통' refers to the pain symptom.

examples.ko: 날씨가 추우니까 웃옷을 하나 더 입어요.
examples.en: It's cold, so put on one more outer layer.
Take off your jacket and hang it on the chair.
I got rained on, and my jacket is all wet.
This jacket goes well with the pants.
It was hot, so I worked with my outer layer off.
I put the key in my jacket pocket.

explain: 맨 겉에 입는 옷을 말해요. 바지나 치마와 짝이 되는 '윗옷(상의)'과 철자가 달라서 헷갈리기 쉬워요. 일상에서는 '겉옷'이라고도 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It means the outermost garment you wear. It is easy to confuse with '윗옷' (a top, as opposed to pants or a skirt) because the spelling differs. In daily speech people also often say '겉옷'.

examples.ko: 저는 위장병 때문에 매운 음식을 못 먹어요.
examples.en: I can't eat spicy food because of my stomach trouble.
My father has suffered from a stomach disorder for a long time.

examples.ko: 스트레스가 심하면 위장병이 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: Heavy stress can cause stomach trouble.
Regular meals are important for stomach trouble.
I took stomach medicine and felt a bit better.
My friend was hospitalized for a stomach disorder.

explain: 위나 장이 오래 안 좋은 상태를 넓게 부르는 말이에요. 병명이 아니라 '위장 쪽 병'이라는 느낌이라서 일상에서 많이 써요. 병원에서는 '위염', '장염'처럼 더 정확한 이름을 말해요.
explain_en: It is a broad term for long-term stomach or bowel problems. It is not a precise diagnosis but a general 'stomach-area illness', so it is common in daily talk. Hospitals use more exact names like '위염' or '장염'.

examples.ko: 당뇨가 있는 사람은 인슐린 주사를 맞아요.
examples.en: People with diabetes take insulin shots.
When there isn't enough insulin, blood sugar rises.
The doctor prescribed insulin for me.

examples.ko: 인슐린은 몸에서 혈당을 조절하는 역할을 해요.
examples.en: Insulin plays a role in controlling blood sugar in the body.
I carry an insulin pen in my bag.

examples.ko: 저녁 먹기 전에 인슐린으로 혈당을 맞춰요.
examples.en: Before dinner, I adjust my blood sugar with insulin.

explain: '당뇨', '혈당'과 늘 같이 나오는 의학 단어예요. '인슐린 주사', '인슐린 저항성', '인슐린이 나오다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 본인이나 가족이 당뇨일 때 주로 들어요.
explain_en: This medical word almost always appears with '당뇨' (diabetes) and '혈당' (blood sugar). It is used in '인슐린 주사' (insulin shot), '인슐린 저항성' (insulin resistance), and '인슐린이 나오다' (insulin is secreted). In daily talk you mostly hear it when you or a family member has diabetes.

examples.en: If you can't sleep, your concentration drops.

examples.ko: 나이가 들수록 기억력이 저하하는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I think memory declines as you get older.
The factory is old, so production efficiency fell.
With the weather getting worse, the ratings will drop.
When my grades fell, my teacher was worried.

examples.ko: 약을 너무 오래 먹으면 면역력이 저하하기도 해요.
examples.en: Taking medicine for too long can also weaken immunity.

explain: 저하하다는 능력, 기능, 수준이 전보다 나빠지거나 떨어질 때 써요. '집중력', '기억력', '면역력', '효율'처럼 눈에 안 보이는 능력과 잘 어울려요. 말할 때는 '떨어지다'가 더 흔하고 저하하다는 글이나 뉴스에서 더 많이 보여요.
explain_en: 저하하다 is used when ability, function, or level gets worse than before. It goes well with invisible capacities such as '집중력', '기억력', '면역력', and '효율'. In speech '떨어지다' is more common, while 저하하다 is more typical of writing and the news.

examples.ko: 그가 말할 때마다 턱뼈가 움직이는 게 보여요.
examples.en: I can see his jawbone move every time he talks.
I badly injured my jawbone when I fell.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 턱뼈 사진을 보여 주셨어요.
examples.en: The doctor showed me an X-ray of my jawbone.
They say the jawbone where the tooth was pulled has weakened.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 턱뼈가 각져서 인상이 강해 보여요.
examples.en: That actor has an angular jawbone, so he looks strong-featured.
I saw a fossil of an animal's jawbone at the museum.

explain: 몸의 '턱'은 얼굴 아랫부분 전체를 말하고, '턱뼈'는 그 안의 뼈를 가리켜요. 병원이나 치과에서 자주 들을 수 있어요. 사람 얼굴의 윤곽을 말할 때는 '턱선'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: '턱' is the whole lower part of the face, and '턱뼈' points to the bone inside it. You often hear it at hospitals and dentists. When talking about the outline of a face, people also say '턱선'.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 밥 먹을 때 틀니를 끼세요.
examples.en: Grandpa puts in his dentures when he eats.

examples.ko: 틀니가 잘 맞지 않아서 치과에 갔어요.
examples.en: The dentures didn't fit well, so I went to the dentist.
My father got new dentures last year.

examples.ko: 자기 전에 틀니를 깨끗이 닦아야 해요.
examples.en: You have to clean your dentures before going to bed.
Because of the dentures, avoid hard food.
When you get dentures, speaking is awkward at first.

explain: 의학 용어로는 '의치'라고 하지만 일상에서는 '틀니'라고 해요. 몇 개만 끼우는 건 '부분 틀니', 전체는 '완전 틀니'라고 해요. 어르신에게는 '틀니를 하시다'처럼 높여요.
explain_en: The medical term is 의치, but in daily life people say 틀니. A partial set is 부분 틀니 and a full set is 완전 틀니. For elders you raise it: '틀니를 하시다'.

examples.en: The complications of diabetes are scary.

examples.ko: 수술 뒤에 합병증이 생기지 않아서 다행이에요.
examples.en: I am glad no complications appeared after the surgery.

examples.ko: 감기를 오래 두면 합병증으로 이어질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you leave a cold alone for long, it can lead to complications.
The doctor told me to watch out for complications.

examples.ko: 할아버지는 합병증 때문에 한 달 더 입원하셨어요.
examples.en: My grandfather stayed in the hospital another month because of complications.

examples.ko: 합병증을 막으려면 꾸준히 약을 먹어야 해요.
examples.en: To prevent complications, you have to keep taking your medicine.

explain: 합병증은 한 병 때문에 다른 병이나 증상이 따라서 생기는 것이에요. '합병증이 생기다', '합병증을 막다', '합병증이 오다'처럼 써요. '당뇨 합병증'처럼 병 이름과 붙여 많이 말해요.
explain_en: Hapbyeongjeung is a second illness or symptom that follows from a first illness. It pairs with 생기다, 막다, and 오다, as in 합병증이 생기다. It is often attached to a disease name, as in 당뇨 합병증.

en: to wear out; to be tattered; to become shabby

examples.en: The clothes wore out from long use.
The shoe soles wore through, so I bought new ones.

examples.ko: 이 가방은 자주 들면 모서리가 해져요.
examples.en: If you carry this bag often, the corners fray.
It's a shame to throw away worn socks.

examples.ko: 책 표지가 해지기 전에 커버를 씌웠어요.
examples.en: I put a cover on before the book jacket wore out.
I wore the jeans until the knees wore out.

explain: 옷, 신발, 가방처럼 오래 써서 닳고 찢어질 때 써요. '낡다'는 오래되어 허름해진 상태이고, '해지다'는 천이나 가죽이 닳아서 올이 풀리거나 구멍이 나는 변화예요. '해가 지다'와 소리는 비슷하지만 달라요.
explain_en: It is used when clothes, shoes, or bags wear down and fray from long use. 낡다 is the general state of being old and shabby, while 해지다 is the change of fabric or leather wearing thin or tearing. It sounds similar to 해가 지다 (the sun sets) but is unrelated.
